audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers give Ryze all seven stages, while the page's own whys[] hand Nautilus levels 2 through first item ('He owns this window by threat alone', 'He controls the range game', 'He still wins a hook-combo trade'). Packet chart and the already-applied mirror agree with the prose.
audit.why: 49.22% over 1032 games is not a Ryze-owns-everything lane. The mirror settled it as Level 1 Skill, Levels 2 through first item Nautilus, 2+ items Ryze; sides are shared between the two directions, so restating it from Ryze's side is identical with inverted ratings.
audit.corrected: Skill / Nautilus / Nautilus / Nautilus / Nautilus / Nautilus / Ryze, proposed as matched full+content pairs with ratings flipped.

audit.why: Four spikes present in the right order: Lvl 2 (Dredge Line arrives), Lvl 3-5 (hook combo is the kill), 1st item, 2+ items. Ryze's spike is mana items; Nautilus's is levels plus tank items.
audit.corrected: Kept; spikes[0].text corrected only for the ability slot error, and three phases[].why lines rewritten to stop contradicting the corrected sides.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[0].text calls Riptide his W and wants.foe[0] repeats 'Riptide (W)'. Riptide is E (7/6.5/6/5.5/5s, 600 range); W is Titan's Wrath, a 12s shield. Two applicable interactions never reach the page: Titan's Wrath absorbing the burst window, and Dredge Line pulling Nautilus to terrain to cut a retreat Ryze has no dash to make.
audit.why: Kit is explicit: W grants a shield and damage-over-time autos; E is the three-wave slow. Dredge Line is 1150 range on 14/13/12/11/10s and collides with terrain to pull Nautilus toward it. Mirror-confirmed from the other side: Depth Charge (120/100/80s) is point-click homing, so Realm Warp's delayed portal does not shake it, and an unfluxed Rune Prison is only a slow.
audit.corrected: Titan's Wrath (W) is the 12s shield to bait; Riptide (E) is the slow; Staggering Blow (P) roots on his first attack; Dredge Line reaches 1150 and can also anchor him to terrain behind you.

edits.before: Phase Rush turns his engage into your trade window — combo, proc the speed, and walk away untouched.
edits.after: Dredge Line is 1150 range on 10-14s — outside it you're free, inside it his root chain starts.

edits.before: Realm Warp opens flanks and escapes, and your EQ DPS now duels most tops on their cooldown gaps.
edits.after: Realm Warp is macro only — Depth Charge homes point-click, and the portal's delay never shakes it.

edits.before: Rod of Ages ends the HP problem — your short trades become favourable on raw math.
edits.after: Rod of Ages helps, but his tank items outpace it — he still wins the hook trade.

edits.before: Nautilus hits W (Riptide) + passive root on autos — every auto he lands roots you in place, and you have no gap-close to punish him before he walks away.
edits.after: Nautilus gets Titan's Wrath (W) shield and Riptide (E) slows, and Staggering Blow roots on his first auto — you have no dash to punish him before he walks away.

edits.before: Land Dredge Line (Q hook) to pull you into passive root range, then layer Riptide (W) for a full multi-hit trade sequence
edits.after: Land Dredge Line (Q, 1150 range) to pull you into Staggering Blow root range, then layer Riptide (E) for the full trade

edits.before: That’s Nautilus’s bread-and-butter play — deny it and they run out of answers.
edits.after: Titan's Wrath shields the burst — bait the 12s shield before you commit.

edits.before: Nautilus spends Dredge Line (Hook) early — the closest thing this matchup has to a guarantee.
edits.after: Dredge Line also anchors him to terrain behind you — hold Flash for the cut-off.

notes: Chart proposed as one atomic group across both layers, matching the applied mirror (mel-style disagreement avoided). diff/diffRating left at EVEN / 4/10 — the mirror deliberately left its side alone given its 18-game sample, and changing only this side would create a new contradiction.
